chapter: HOT Category Puzzles — Uncertain Seating Arrangement Based

question_level_cross_database_deduplicat.method: Compared full shared directions, question meaning, and solved arrangements against all 40 target-chapter rows in a read-only local transaction. Inspected the highest text-overlap records; these are self-authored north-facing rows with six named people separated by a fixed two-seat gap, while the PDF puzzles use different clues/variables, row lengths, and asked relations. No equivalent puzzle set/question was found.

entries.shared_directions: A north-facing row has an unknown number of people. C is at an end and has two people between it and B. The number to the right of G equals the number to its left. The remaining copied clue says the number between F and C equals the number between F and D.
entries.question: Who is sitting third to the right of F?
entries.reasoning: Held without selecting either version of the shared clue. The two source pages conflict (D–G on p.5; D–C on p.6), so the written puzzle is not a single consistent specification.
entries.printed_key_or_annotation: No reliable answer can be verified from the contradictory source.

entries.shared_directions: An unknown-length north-facing row. M is eighth left of J; N is fourth right of K; O immediately left of P; L is exactly midway between K and J; P is third from the right end. The number between J and P equals that between K and J. Exactly ten people are left of J; six people are between N and O; the number between M and J equals that between Q and J.
entries.question: How many persons are sitting in the row?
entries.reasoning: J has exactly ten people to its left, so J=11. The K/J gap equals the J/P gap; the midpoint clue puts L midway between K and J. The K=17 branch would force P=17 too, so it collides; thus K=5,L=8. P is six positions right of J at 17, so n=19. O=P−1=16, N=K+4=9, and six people lie between N and O. M=3 and Q=19 satisfy the final equal-gap clue.
entries.review_note: The complete satisfying placement is M3,K5,L8,N9,J11,O16,P17,Q19; there are 19 seats.

retired_records.question_text:
Original Practice Question — A row has an unknown total of 12, 13, 14, or 15 people, all facing north. The six named people A, B, C, D, E, F are present, and every other seat is occupied by a different, unnamed person. Number seats from the left starting at 1. Shared clues: A sits second from the left. B sits exactly two seats to the right of A; C sits exactly two seats to the right of B; D sits exactly two seats to the right of C; E sits exactly two seats to the right of D; F sits exactly two seats to the right of E.

Question: Who occupies seat 11?
retired_records.explanation: The clues place the six named people at seats A=2, B=4, C=6, D=8, E=10, F=12. These positions fit every permitted row length 12–15; unnamed participants fill the other seats. The requested fact is the same in all four valid row lengths: An unnamed participant.
